scenario: Relative-time mechanisms read the monotonic clock only (LTIM.2.8.2): stepping the wall clock back an hour and then forward two neither closes, re-opens nor re-fires a `dwell` gate. Drives the tick re-evaluation of a single-pattern `where` reading `dwell`, with the harness's `wall_set` step (mock wall clock alone, NTST.3.1). Pin: set 0; wall_set 2001-09-09T01:46:40Z; assert Ping; advance 5_s, pump (fires); wall_set one hour earlier, pump; wall_set one hour later than the first, pump; advance 1_s, pump. Messages are ['fired'] exactly once. A runtime whose `dwell` reads the wall clock closes the gate on the backward step (the dwell goes negative) and re-opens it on the forward one, a new match that fires again: ['fired', 'fired']. The backward step alone cannot tell the two apart, because nothing would re-open the gate.
rules_ds:
schema Ping scope logical:
    k: String key

rule held:
    Ping p where p.dwell >= 3_s
->
    log critical "fired"
